situation.roe_position: ROE has swung with the underwriting cycle: the combined ratio was 107.7% in 2023, 101.1% in 2024 and 99.0% in 2025, and ROE moved from 2.3% to 12.0% over that span. 2026 is weaker at the nine-month mark because of two Q1 winter storms (nine-month combined ratio 101.7%), although Q3 improved to 96.3%. Part of the 2025 ROE came from investment gains and strong partnership income, and a softening market now limits pricing.
situation.why: 2025 ROE of 0.1198 sits at the top of the 6-year range (median 0.0879), helped by a benign catastrophe year, rate increases earning in and realized gains. The company pays out roughly two-thirds of earnings as dividends and carries only 50,000 of debt, so regulatory capital does not appear to bind book growth. The Massachusetts dividend limits on the subsidiary are a general constraint, not an evidenced binding one. A pending $105 cash merger overrides any standalone path, so these inputs describe the standalone business.

situation.roe_position: The 2025 return of 0.1198 was lifted by earned rate increases, a 99.0% combined ratio and realized gains. 2026 is weaker: two severe Q1 winter storms pushed the nine-month combined ratio to 101.7% and nine-month net income fell to $50.2 million from $79.1 million. Q3 recovered to a 96.3% combined ratio, and investment income is at a record. Premiums are shrinking in a softer market and rate gains are slowing, so I expect a return around the 6-year median, not the 2025 peak.
situation.why: Debt is only $50 million against $856 million of equity, and the company pays out most of its earnings in dividends, so book equity grows slowly by choice, not because of capital limits. Subsidiary dividends are subject to Massachusetts law, but nothing in the packet shows that binding. Year 1 book equity shrinks because unrealized bond losses (accumulated other comprehensive loss) widened sharply. The Mapfre merger at $105 per share is a separate matter; these inputs describe the standalone book and return.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K business and MD&A sections.
business_model.claim: Safety is a property and casualty insurer. It sells private passenger auto, commercial auto and homeowners insurance, plus smaller lines such as dwelling fire, umbrella and business owner policies. Private passenger auto is the largest line at 54.9% of 2025 direct written premiums, followed by homeowners at 25.2% and commercial auto at 15.2%.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K tables and risk factors.

quotes: A majority of our direct written premiums are currently generated in Massachusetts.

business_model.claim: Customers are reached exclusively through independent agents. The 10-K counts 797 agents in 1,063 locations during 2025. Agents are paid commissions and profit-sharing programs, and the company tries to be one of the top two carriers in each agency.
